t: Ravi obtained 70 and 75 marks in first two unit tests. Then, the minimum marks he should get in the third test to have an average of at least 60 marks, are
s:
Let Ravi got x marks in third unit test. ∴ Average marks obtained by Ravi =( Sum of marks in all tests )/( Number of tests ) =(70+75+x)/3=(145+x)/3
Now, it is given that he wants to obtain an average of at least 60 marks. At least 60 marks means that the marks should be greater than or equal to 60. i.e. (145+x)/3≥60
⇒145+x≥60×3
⇒145+x≥180
Now, transferring the term 145 to R.H.S., x≥180−145⇒x≥35
i.e. Ravi should get greater than or equal to 35 marks in third unit test to get an average of at least 60 marks.
∴ Minimum marks Ravi should get =35.

t: A man wants to cut three lengths from a single piece of board of length 91 cm. The second length is to be 3 cm longer than the shortest and the third length is to be twice as long as the shortest. The possible length of the shortest board, if the third piece is to be at least 5 cm longer than the second, is
s:
Let the shortest side be xcm. Then, by given condition, second length =x+3 cm
Third length =2×cm
Also given, total length =91 Hence, sum of all the three lengths should be less than or equal to 91 ⇒x+x+3+2x≤91⇒4x+3≤91
Subtracting (−3) to each term, −3+4x+3≤91−3 ⇒4x≤88⇒4x/4≤88/4⇒x≤88/4
⇒ x≤22 cm …
Again, given that Third length ≥ Second length +5 ⇒ 2x≥(x+3)+5⇒2x≥x+(3+5)
Transferring the term x to L.H.S., 2x−x≥8⇒x≥8 …
From equations (i) and (ii), length of shortest board should be greater than or equal to 8 but less than or equal to 22, i.e., 8≤x≤22
o: greater than or equal to 8 cm but less than or equal to 22 cm

The value of (1+2log₃2)/((1+log₃2)²)+(log₆2)² is
s:
Concept:
Using change of base, 1 + log₃2 = log₃3 + log₃2 = log₃6. 
Thus, log₆2 = log₃2 / log₃6 = log₃2 / (1 + log₃2). 
The expression simplifies to a perfect square identity divided by itself, giving a constant value independent of the base.

Calculation:
Let x = log₃2.
Then 1 + log₃2 = 1 + x.
Using the base change theorem:
log₆2 = log₃2 / log₃6 = x / (1 + x).

Substitute these into the expression:
E = (1 + 2x)/(1 + x)² + [x/(1 + x)]²
E = (1 + 2x + x²)/(1 + x)²
E = (1 + x)²/(1 + x)² = 1

Options (A), (B), and (C) are incorrect as the algebraic terms reduce directly to unity.
